sanskrit: tatreyam arthamātrā me bhīmasena vivakṣitā naikāntasiddhir mantavyā kurubhiḥ saha saṃyuge
english: O Bhīmasena, this much is what I wish to convey: victory in battle against the Kurus is not to be considered absolutely certain.

sanskrit: nātipraṇītaraśmiḥ syāt tathā bhavati paryaye viṣādam arched glāniṃ vā etadarthaṃ bravīmi te
english: One should not draw the reins too tight, for in a reversal of fortune that very effort leads to despair or exhaustion — it is for this reason that I speak thus to you.

sanskrit: śvobhūte dhṛtarāṣṭrasya samīpaṃ prāpya pāṇḍava yatiṣye praśamaṃ kartuṃ yuṣmadartham ahāpayan
english: O Pāṇḍava, when tomorrow comes and I approach Dhṛtarāṣṭra, I shall strive to bring about peace on your behalf, without sacrificing your interests.

sanskrit: śamaṃ cet te kariṣyanti tato 'nantaṃ yaśo mama bhavatāṃ ca kṛtaḥ kāmas teṣāṃ ca śreya uttamam
english: If they agree to peace, then boundless glory shall be mine, your desire shall be fulfilled, and the highest good shall accrue to them as well.

sanskrit: te ced abhinivekṣyanti nābhyupaiṣyanti me vacaḥ kuravo yuddham evātra raudraṃ karma bhaviṣyati
english: But if the Kurus persist in their course and do not accept my words, then there shall be dreadful war and terrible deeds.

sanskrit: asmin yuddhe bhīmasena tvayi bhāraḥ samāhitaḥ dhūr arjunena dhāryā syād voḍhavya itaro janaḥ
english: O Bhīmasena, in this war the chief burden rests on you; the yoke is to be borne by Arjuna, and all others shall follow their lead.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi yantā bībhatsor bhavitā saṃyuge sati dhanaṃjayasyaiṣa kāmo na hi yuddhaṃ na kāmaye
english: I shall be the charioteer of Arjuna in the battle — this is the wish of Dhanañjaya himself; for I do not desire war.

sanskrit: tasmād āśaṅkamāno 'haṃ vṛkodara matiṃ tava tudann aklībayā vācā tejas te samadīpayam
english: Therefore, O Vṛkodara, being apprehensive, I have been piercing your mind and rousing your valour with bold words to kindle your spirit.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca uktaṃ yudhiṣṭhireṇaiva yāvad vācyaṃ janārdana tava vākyaṃ tu me śrutvā pratibhāti paraṃtapa
english: Arjuna said: O Janārdana, O scorcher of foes, Yudhiṣṭhira has said all that was to be said; but having heard your words, a reflection arises in my mind.

sanskrit: naiva praśamam atra tvaṃ manyase sukaraṃ prabho lobhād vā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dainyād vā samupasthitāt
english: O lord, you yourself do not consider peace here to be easy — whether because of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's greed or the wretchedness that has come upon him.

sanskrit: aphalaṃ manyase cāpi puruṣasya parākramam na cāntareṇa karmāṇi pauruṣeṇa phalodayaḥ
english: And yet you hold that human valour is fruitless, and that actions do not bear fruit without manly effort.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ tathā ca na tathaiva ca na caitad evaṃ draṣṭavyam asādhyam iti kiṃ cana
english: This speech you have given is in one sense true and in another not quite so; yet nothing in it should be regarded as unachievable.

sanskrit: kiṃ caitan manyase kṛcchram asmākaṃ pāpam āditaḥ kurvanti teṣāṃ karmāṇi yeṣāṃ nāsti phalodayaḥ
english: And do you regard our hardship as the sin from the beginning? Only the deeds of those bear no fruit who have sinned.

sanskrit: saṃpādyamānaṃ samyak ca syāt karma saphalaṃ prabho sa tathā kṛṣṇa vartasva yathā śarma bhavet paraiḥ
english: O lord, an action rightly performed shall surely be fruitful; therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, act in such a way that the enemy may find peace.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca bhavān paramakaḥ suhṛt surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca yathā vīra prajāpatiḥ
english: O hero, you are the supreme well-wisher of both the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, just as Prajāpati is to the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca pratipatsva nirāmayam asmaddhitam anuṣṭhātuṃ na manye tava duṣkaram
english: Secure the welfare of both the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas; I do not think it difficult for you to accomplish what is good for us.

sanskrit: evaṃ cet kāryatām eti kāryaṃ tava janārdana gamanād evam eva tvaṃ kariṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: O Janārdana, if the mission becomes accomplished thus, you shall achieve it by your very going there — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: cikīrṣitam athānyat te tasmin vīra durātmani bhaviṣyati tathā sarvaṃ yathā tava cikīrṣitam
english: And whatever else you intend regarding that wicked one, O hero, all shall come to pass exactly as you desire.

sanskrit: śarma taiḥ saha vā no 'stu tava vā yac cikīrṣitam vicāryamāṇo yaḥ kāmas tava kṛṣṇa sa no guruḥ
english: Whether there be peace with them or not, whatever is your purpose — when carefully considered, O Kṛṣṇa, your desire is our highest authority.

sanskrit: na sa nārhati duṣṭātmā vadhaṃ sasutabāndhavaḥ yena dharmasute dṛṣṭvā na sā śrīr upamarṣitā
english: That wicked-souled one, along with his sons and kinsmen, surely deserves death — he who could not tolerate the prosperity of the son of Dharma even when witnessed.

sanskrit: yac cāpy apaśyatopāyaṃ dharmiṣṭhaṃ madhusūdana upāyena nṛśaṃsena hṛtā durdyūtadevinā
english: And he who, O Madhusūdana, seeing no righteous means, seized what was ours through a cruel stratagem — by winning at a crooked game of dice.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi puruṣo jātaḥ kṣatriyeṣu dhanurdharaḥ samāhūto nivarteta prāṇatyāge 'py upasthite
english: How can a man born among Kṣatriyas, bearing a bow, turn back when challenged, even when the surrender of life itself is at hand?

sanskrit: adharmeṇa jitān dṛṣṭvā vane pravrajitāṃs tathā vadhyatāṃ mama vārṣṇeya nirgato 'sau suyodhanaḥ
english: Having seen us defeated by unrighteous means and forced to wander in the forest, that Suyodhana has become fit to be slain by me, O Vārṣṇeya.

sanskrit: na caitad adbhutaṃ kṛṣṇa mitrārthe yac cikīrṣasi kriyā kathaṃ nu mukhyā syān mṛdunā vetareṇa vā
english: O Kṛṣṇa, there is nothing wondrous in what you wish to do for the sake of a friend. How can the foremost action be achieved — whether by gentle means or by other means?

sanskrit: atha vā manyase jyāyān vadhas teṣām anantaram tad eva kriyatām āśu na vicāryam atas tvayā
english: Or if you deem their immediate slaughter to be superior, then let that be done at once — you need not deliberate further.

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā tena draupadī pāpabuddhinā parikliṣṭā sabhāmadhye tac ca tasyāpi marṣitam
english: For you know how Draupadī was tormented in the assembly hall by that evil-minded one — and even that was endured by her.

sanskrit: sa nāma samyag varteta pāṇḍaveṣv iti mādhava na me saṃjāyate buddhir bījam uptam ivoṣare
english: O Mādhava, I cannot bring myself to believe that he would conduct himself rightly toward the Pāṇḍavas — like seed sown on barren ground.

sanskrit: tasmād yan manyase yuktaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yad dhitam tad āśu kuru vārṣṇeya yan naḥ kāryam anantaram
english: Therefore, O Vārṣṇeya, whatever you deem proper and beneficial for the Pāṇḍavas — do that quickly; whatever must be done for us, do it without delay.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi pāṇḍava sarvaṃ tv idaṃ samāyattaṃ bībhatso karmaṇor dvayoḥ
english: The Lord said: O mighty-armed Pāṇḍava, it is as you say; yet, O Bībhatsu, all of this depends upon the two kinds of action — human and divine.

sanskrit: kṣetraṃ hi rasavac chuddhaṃ karṣakeṇopapāditam ṛte varṣaṃ na kaunteya jātu nirvartayet phalam
english: A field, though rich in sap and well prepared by the farmer, O Kaunteya, will never yield a harvest without rain.

sanskrit: tatra vai pauruṣaṃ brūyur āsekaṃ yatnakāritam tatra cāpi dhruvaṃ paśyec choṣaṇaṃ daivakāritam
english: There, men call the irrigation and cultivation human effort; but there too one can clearly see the drying up caused by fate.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ niścitaṃ buddhyā pūrvair api mahātmabhiḥ daive ca mānuṣe caiva saṃyuktaṃ lokakāraṇam
english: This has been ascertained by wise men of old: the cause of things in the world lies in the combination of divine and human action.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tat kariṣyāmi paraṃ puruṣakārataḥ daivaṃ tu na mayā śakyaṃ karma kartuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I shall do what is supremely possible through human effort; but the working of fate I cannot control in any way.

sanskrit: sa hi dharmaṃ ca satyaṃ ca tyaktvā carati durmatiḥ na hi saṃtapyate tena tathārūpeṇa karmaṇā
english: For that evil-minded one has abandoned both dharma and truth and conducts himself accordingly; he does not grieve over deeds of such a nature.

sanskrit: tāṃ cāpi buddhiṃ pāpiṣṭhāṃ vardhayanty asya mantriṇaḥ śakuniḥ sūtaputraś ca bhrātā duḥśāsanas tathā
english: And his counsellors — Śakuni, the son of a charioteer, and his brother Duḥśāsana — encourage and strengthen that sinful resolve of his.

sanskrit: sa hi tyāgena rājyasya na śamaṃ samupeṣyati antareṇa vadhāt pārtha sānubandhaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: O Pārtha, Suyodhana, together with his allies, will not attain peace by relinquishing the kingdom; short of his slaughter there is no other way.

sanskrit: na cāpi praṇipātena tyaktum icchati dharmarāṭ yācyamānas tu rājyaṃ sa na pradāsyati durmatiḥ
english: Nor will that evil-minded king of dharma consent to give up the kingdom even when entreated; even when begged, he will not give it.

sanskrit: na tu manye sa tad vācyo yad yudhiṣṭhiraśāsanam uktaṃ prayojanaṃ tatra dharmarājena bhārata
english: Yet I do not think he is the one who should be told the instruction of Yudhiṣṭhira — the purpose has already been stated there by the king of dharma, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tathā pāpas tu tat sarvaṃ na kariṣyati kauravaḥ tasmiṃś cākriyamāṇe 'sau lokavadhyo bhaviṣyati
english: Yet that sinful Kaurava will not do all of that; and when he refuses to act accordingly, he shall become worthy of death in the eyes of the world.

sanskrit: mama cāpi sa vadhyo vai jagataś cāpi bhārata yena kaumārake yūyaṃ sarve viprakṛtās tathā
english: And he is deserving of death at my hands as well, O Bharata — and in the eyes of the world — for he wronged all of you even in your boyhood.

sanskrit: vipraluptaṃ ca vo rājyaṃ nṛśaṃsena durātmanā na copaśāmyate pāpaḥ śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhire
english: Your kingdom has been seized by that cruel, wicked-souled one; and the sinner is not appeased even when he beholds the prosperity of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: asakṛc cāpy ahaṃ tena tvatkṛte pārtha bheditaḥ na mayā tad gṛhītaṃ ca pāpaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam
english: And more than once he has tried to sow discord between us for your sake, O Pārtha; but I did not accept that sinful design of his.

sanskrit: jānāsi hi mahābāho tvam apy asya paraṃ matam priyaṃ cikīrṣamāṇaṃ ca dharmarājasya mām api
english: You know well, O mighty-armed one, his deepest intent; and you also know that I desire what is dear to the king of dharma and to myself.

sanskrit: sa jānaṃs tasya cātmānaṃ mama caiva paraṃ matam ajānann iva cākasmād arjunādyābhiśaṅkase
english: Knowing his own nature and my supreme intent, you nevertheless suspect me — as though unknowing — along with Arjuna and others, without any cause.

sanskrit: yac cāpi paramaṃ divyaṃ tac cāpy avagataṃ tvayā vidhānavihitaṃ pārtha kathaṃ śarma bhavet paraiḥ
english: And that which is supremely divine — you have also understood that, O Pārtha — ordained by fate; how then could peace come from the enemy?

sanskrit: yat tu vācā mayā śakyaṃ karmaṇā cāpi pāṇḍava kariṣye tad ahaṃ pārtha na tv āśaṃse śamaṃ paraiḥ
english: Whatever I am able to do by word and by deed, O Pāṇḍava, that I shall do, O Pārtha; but I do not expect peace from the enemy.

sanskrit: kathaṃ goharaṇe brūyād icchañ śarma tathāvidham yācyamāno 'pi bhīṣmeṇa saṃvatsaragate 'dhvani
english: How could one who desires such peace speak of stealing cattle? — even when Bhīṣma pleaded with him, even after a year had passed.

sanskrit: tadaiva te parābhūtā yadā saṃkalpitās tvayā lavaśaḥ kṣaṇaśaś cāpi na ca tuṣṭaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: You were already defeated the moment you resolved to divide things bit by bit and moment by moment — and still Suyodhana was not satisfied.

sanskrit: sarvathā tu mayā kāryaṃ dharmarājasya śāsanam vibhāvyaṃ tasya bhūyaś ca karma pāpaṃ durātmanaḥ
english: Yet in every way I must carry out the command of the king of dharma, and once again make manifest the sinful deeds of that wicked-souled one.

sanskrit: nakula uvāca uktaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vākyaṃ dharmarājena mādhava dharmajñena vadānyena dharmayuktaṃ ca tattvataḥ
english: Nakula said: O Mādhava, the king of dharma — knower of dharma and generous of speech — has spoken at length and in conformity with truth and righteousness.

sanskrit: matam ājñāya rājñaś ca bhīmasenena mādhava saṃśamo bāhuvīryaṃ ca khyāpitaṃ mādhavātmanaḥ
english: O Mādhava, understanding the king's intention, Bhīmasena has made known both the desire for peace and the strength of his arms.

sanskrit: tathaiva phalgunenāpi yad uktaṃ tat tvayā śrutam ātmanaś ca mataṃ vīra kathitaṃ bhavatāsakṛt
english: Likewise, what Phalguna has said — you have heard it; and your own opinion, O hero, has been expressed by you more than once.

sanskrit: sarvam etad atikramya śrutvā paramataṃ bhavān yat prāptakālaṃ manyethās tat kuryāḥ puruṣottama
english: O best of men, having heard all this and setting it aside, whatever you consider timely — do that.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tasmin nimitte hi mataṃ bhavati keśava prāptakālaṃ manuṣyeṇa svayaṃ kāryam ariṃdama
english: O Keśava, O subduer of foes, in each specific circumstance what is timely must be done by a person of his own accord.

sanskrit: anyathā cintito hy arthaḥ punar bhavati so 'nyathā anityamatayo loke narāḥ puruṣasattama
english: O best of men, a matter thought of one way turns out differently — men in this world are of changeable minds.

sanskrit: anyathā buddhayo hy āsann asmāsu vanavāsiṣu adṛśyeṣv anyathā kṛṣṇa dṛśyeṣu punar anyathā
english: Their dispositions toward us were one way when we were dwelling in the forest unseen, O Kṛṣṇa, and altogether different when we were visible — and now different again.

sanskrit: asmākam api vārṣṇeya vane vicaratāṃ tadā na tathā praṇayo rājye yathā saṃprati vartate
english: O Vārṣṇeya, even our own attachment to the kingdom was not as great when we were wandering in the forest as it is now.

sanskrit: nivṛttavanavāsān naḥ śrutvā vīra samāgatāḥ akṣauhiṇyo hi saptemās tvatprasādāj janārdana
english: O hero, upon hearing that our forest-exile had ended, seven akshauhinis have assembled to our cause, O Janārdana, through your grace.

sanskrit: imān hi puruṣavyāghrān acintyabalapauruṣān āttaśastrān raṇe dṛṣṭvā na vyathed iha kaḥ pumān
english: Seeing these tiger-like men, of inconceivable strength and valour, who have taken up their weapons for battle — what man here would not tremble?

sanskrit: sa bhavān kurumadhye taṃ sāntvapūrvaṃ bhayānvitam brūyād vākyaṃ yathā mando na vyatheta suyodhanaḥ
english: May you, in the midst of the Kurus, speak words first with conciliation, so that even the dull-witted Suyodhana, filled with fear, does not tremble.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhīmasenaṃ bībhatsuṃ cāparājitam sahadevaṃ ca māṃ caiva tvāṃ ca rāmaṃ ca keśava
english: O Keśava — Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena, the unconquered Bībhatsu, Sahadeva and myself, you and Rāma as well —

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ ca mahāvīryaṃ virāṭaṃ ca sahātmajam drupadaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam
english: — and the greatly valiant Sātyaki, Virāṭa with his son, Drupada with his ministers, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata —

sanskrit: kāśirājaṃ ca vikrāntaṃ dhṛṣṭaketuṃ ca cedipam māṃsaśoṇitabhṛn martyaḥ pratiyudhyeta ko yudhi
english: — and the valiant king of Kāśi, and Dhṛṣṭaketu of the Cedis — what mortal, made of flesh and blood, could stand against these in battle?

sanskrit: sa bhavān gamanād eva sādhayiṣyaty asaṃśayam iṣṭam arthaṃ mahābāho dharmarājasya kevalam
english: O mighty-armed one, you will undoubtedly accomplish the desired purpose of the king of dharma by your very going there alone.

sanskrit: viduraś caiva bhīṣmaś ca droṇaś ca sahabāhlikaḥ śreyaḥ samarthā vijñātum ucyamānaṃ tvayānagha
english: O sinless one, Vidura, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Bahlika are capable of discerning what is good when it is spoken by you.

sanskrit: te cainam anuneṣyanti dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janādhipam taṃ ca pāpasamācāraṃ sahāmātyaṃ suyodhanam
english: And they will prevail upon King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and upon that wicked-actioned Suyodhana together with his ministers.

sanskrit: śrotā cārthasya viduras tvaṃ ca vaktā janārdana kam ivārthaṃ vivartantaṃ sthāpayetāṃ na vartmani
english: O Janārdana, with Vidura as the listener and you as the speaker, what matter going astray could the two of you not set on the right path?

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca yad etat kathitaṃ rājñā dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ yathā tu yuddham eva syāt tathā kāryam ariṃdama
english: Sahadeva said: What the king has said is eternal dharma; yet, O subduer of foes, whatever must be done to ensure that war takes place — that should be done.

sanskrit: yadi praśamam iccheyuḥ kuravaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha tathāpi yuddhaṃ dāśārha yojayethāḥ sahaiva taiḥ
english: O Dāśārha, even if the Kurus were to desire peace with the Pāṇḍavas, you should still arrange for war against them.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu dṛṣṭvā pāñcālīṃ tathā kliṣṭāṃ sabhāgatām avadhena praśāmyeta mama manyuḥ suyodhane
english: How indeed can my rage against Suyodhana be quelled without his death, when I have seen Pāñcālī so tormented in that assembly?

sanskrit: yadi bhīmārjunau kṛṣṇa dharmarājaś ca dhārmikaḥ dharmam utsṛjya tenāhaṃ yoddhum icchāmi saṃyuge
english: O Kṛṣṇa, if Bhīma, Arjuna, and the righteous king of dharma were to abandon dharma for his sake, even then I wish to fight him in battle.

sanskrit: sātyakir uvāca satyam āha mahābāho sahadevo mahāmatiḥ duryodhanavadhe śāntis tasya kopasya me bhavet
english: Sātyaki said: O mighty-armed one, the great-minded Sahadeva speaks the truth; my anger would find peace only in the death of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā dṛṣṭvā cīrājinadharān vane tavāpi manyur udbhūto duḥkhitān prekṣya pāṇḍavān
english: For you know how, upon seeing the Pāṇḍavas clad in bark and deerskin in the forest, suffering in misery, your own anger too arose.

sanskrit: tasmān mādrīsutaḥ śūro yad āha puruṣarṣabhaḥ vacanaṃ sarvayodhānāṃ tan mataṃ puruṣottama
english: Therefore, O best of men, what that brave bull among men — the son of Mādrī — has said represents the view of all the warriors.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ vadati vākyaṃ tu yuyudhāne mahāmatau subhīmaḥ siṃhanādo 'bhūd yodhānāṃ tatra sarvaśaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the great-minded Yuyudhāna was speaking thus, a tremendous lion-roar arose from all the warriors gathered there.

sanskrit: sarve hi sarvato vīrās tad vacaḥ pratyapūjayan sādhu sādhv iti śaineyaṃ harṣayanto yuyutsavaḥ
english: All the heroes on every side honoured those words, cheering Shaineyya with cries of "Well done! Well done!" — all eager for battle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājñas tu vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam kṛṣṇā dāśārham āsīnam abravīc chokakarṣitā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the king's words — full of dharma and prudence and full of counsel — Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī), tormented by grief, spoke to Dāśārha who was seated there.

sanskrit: sutā drupadarājasya svasitāyatamūrdhajā saṃpūjya sahadevaṃ ca sātyakiṃ ca mahāratham
english: The daughter of King Drupada, with her long dark hair flowing, having honoured Sahadeva and the great warrior Sātyaki —

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ ca saṃśāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramadurmanāḥ aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā vākyam uvācedaṃ manasvinī
english: — and seeing Bhīmasena composed and still, in deepest anguish, her eyes filled with tears, that noble-minded woman spoke these words:

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahābāho dharmajña madhusūdana yathā nikṛtim āsthāya bhraṃśitāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sukhāt
english: O mighty-armed one, O knower of dharma, O Madhusūdana, you know how the Pāṇḍavas were cast down from their happiness by resorting to treachery.
